title: DSP Mohammed Siraj Reports for Duty, Meets Telangana's New DGP CV Anand
excerpt: India fast bowler Mohammed Siraj has officially donned the Telangana Police uniform as Deputy Superintendent of Police and met the state's newly appointed Director General of Police, CV Anand, in Hyderabad — balancing his dual roles as cricketer and police officer.
body:
Cricketer Turns Officer

India's premier fast bowler Mohammed Siraj has started a new chapter in a career that now spans two uniforms. The Hyderabad-born pacer reported for duty as a Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) in the Telangana Police this week, with photographs of him in full police uniform quickly circulating across social media platforms.

https://x.com/aajtak/status/2079519911177756962

Siraj's first official engagement in his new role included a meeting with CV Anand, who recently began his tenure as Telangana's Director General of Police. During the meeting, Siraj presented Anand with a signed Team India jersey — a gesture that was warmly received on social media.

"It was a pleasure meeting Shri C.V. Anand sir, DGP, Telangana, and extending my best wishes as he begins his tenure as the Director General of Police. Grateful for the warm interaction."

— Mohammed Siraj, via Instagram

From the 2024 World Cup to the Police Force

The prestigious Group-I government post was awarded to Siraj by Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy in recognition of his outstanding contributions to Indian cricket. Siraj was a key member of India's bowling attack during the T20 World Cup 2024 in the Caribbean, where the Men in Blue ended an 11-year wait for an ICC title.

Reddy had announced a residential plot and a government job for Siraj in July 2024 when the pacer called on him after the World Cup triumph. The Telangana government subsequently amended the state's public services Act to allow the appointment, acknowledging that Siraj did not hold the educational qualifications typically required for the Group-I cadre but granting an exemption as part of its policy to encourage sportspersons.

World champion boxer Nikhat Zareen, also from Telangana, received a similar honour from the state government.

Awaiting India Return

Despite taking up the DSP role, Siraj is expected to continue balancing his responsibilities as a police officer with his commitments to the Indian cricket team. The 32-year-old was rested from India's recent tour of the United Kingdom as part of the BCCI's workload management programme.

His absence was felt during the ODI series against England, where India's relatively inexperienced pace attack struggled and the visitors suffered a 2-1 series defeat, according to CricTracker. Siraj was last seen in action during India's one-off Test against Afghanistan, where he continued to lead the pace attack.

Over his international career, Siraj has claimed 140 wickets in Tests, 76 in ODIs, and 17 in T20Is, cementing his place as one of India's most reliable seamers across formats. He also played a key role in helping Gujarat Titans reach the IPL 2026 final with outstanding bowling performances.

What's Next

Siraj is expected to rejoin the Indian squad for the upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka in August, a critical assignment that could determine whether India reaches the World Test Championship final. His return will provide a significant boost to the pace department after the struggles in England.

For now, the fast bowler is making the most of his time in Hyderabad — serving both his state and preparing for his next assignment on the cricket field.
